items.english: By O-Tetsu's own telling, the man set to watch this ferry was an old kobun of hers, Ahodara Gonji. A gambler by trade, and a sham monk.
notes: True identity revealed late here: the blocking monk of p124 was O-Tetsu's man all along. Kept romanisation as in bible.

items.english: It was clear now too that the reason every farmhouse below the Tatsuki bluff had shut its doors to the two of them was that O-Tetsu's word had gone round.
"There, that is the reach I have. And yet you go trailing off on a lovers' road with a snivelling brat like this? A drenched wench and a naked man, there is nothing very stylish in that."
notes: O-Tetsu's jealous register: coarsening and possessive. Kept lovers' road for michiyuki/doubly-suicidal elopement sense without explaining.

items.english: Against a heart burning with blind, sick jealousy, neither reason nor feeling could prevail.
"No, we two are nothing of that sort, neither fond nor anything," Ryujiro set about excusing himself.
"Mistress, please do not think ill of us," Kotora too tried to make her peace.
notes: Kotora addresses O-Tetsu as okami-san; rendered as Mistress to keep placating senior-woman sense in English.

items.english: "Eh? What is this tadpole saying? What right have you to speak straight to a great boss like myself, woman though I am? Hold your tongue and get back," O-Tetsu suddenly thrust Kotora away.
notes: o-tamajakushi is literally tadpole, used as belittling brat. Kept literal.

items.english: Kotora as she fell struck her side on an old stake and went sprawling. O-Tetsu with شع vindictive spite kicked her as she lay and even spat on her. Ryujiro felt at last he could no longer bear this ignorant bullying of O-Tetsu's. With this woman, he thought, he could never make anything of his life. And yet now there was nothing to be done.
"Well, I give up going to Edo. We will go back to Awa from here. There I will clear myself. In any case, my clothes," he said.
notes: Speaker unstated in Japanese; from context it is Ryujiro submitting.

items.english: O-Tetsu's delight at this was beyond all measure.
"Here they are, see. I have them all safe. Come, you will catch cold. Put them on quickly."
She dressed him as a mother dresses a child fresh from the bath. That Ryujiro first drew the small knife from his loincloth and laid it by the roadside goes without saying.
notes: Kept the scale-comedy simile literal. The laying aside of the knife, stated as obvious, is what lets Kotora take it unseen in next paragraph.

data.say: Drafted p207-p218 in brisk kodan voice, keeping jealous registers and the laid-aside knife literal.
